title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Recurrent neural networks have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling. The Transformer replaces recurrent inductive bias with multi-head self-attention, achieving superior translation quality and significant parallelization.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: The Transformer uses stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder. Multi-Head Attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

sections.heading: Experiments
sections.text: On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the big transformer model achieves 28.4 BLEU, improving over the existing best results by over 2.0 BLEU.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: We introduce BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT is designed to pretrain deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Language model pre-training has shown to be effective for improving many natural language processing tasks. We argue that standard unidirectional models are sub-optimal for sentence-level tasks. BERT alleviates the unidirectionality constraint by using a 'masked language model' (MLM) pre-training objective.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.text: BERT is trained on two self-supervised tasks: Masked LM (where 15% of tokens are masked at random) and Next Sentence Prediction (NSP), capturing discourse-level coherence.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: BERT advances the state of the art on eleven NLP benchmarks, obtaining an 80.5% score on GLUE and 93.2 F1 on SQuAD v1.1.

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
abstract: An empirical replication study showing that BERT was significantly undertrained. RoBERTa modifies hyperparameter choices, removes the next sentence prediction objective, and trains on longer sequences.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.text: RoBERTa introduces dynamic masking, removes NSP loss, trains with larger mini-batches (8K) and longer sequences over 160GB of uncompressed text.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: RoBERTa matches or exceeds all post-BERT methods on GLUE, achieving 88.5 GLUE score without multi-task pre-training.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
abstract: T5 casts every language problem into a unified text-to-text format, training on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4).

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: T5 uses an encoder-decoder Transformer. Every task from machine translation to question answering uses identical text input and target tokens.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: T5-11B achieved state-of-the-art results on 18 benchmarks including SuperGLUE and SQuAD.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
abstract: GPT-3 explores scaling language models to 175 billion parameters, demonstrating remarkable in-context few-shot learning capabilities without task-specific gradient updates.

sections.heading: In-Context Learning
sections.text: Scaling models to 175B parameters enables few-shot learning where the model receives task demonstrations solely in prompt context.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: GPT-3 achieves competitive accuracy on trivia, translation, arithmetic, and cloze tests without fine-tuning.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
abstract: We show that retrieval can be practically implemented using dense representations, where embeddings are learned from a small number of questions and passages by a simple dual-encoder architecture.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Open-domain question answering relies on efficient passage retrieval. While BM25 has dominated, DPR trains dual BERT encoders with in-batch negatives to map questions and passages to continuous 768-d vectors.

sections.heading: Dual-Encoder Formulation
sections.text: The retriever computes similarity via dot product: sim(q, p) = E_Q(q)^T E_P(p). Efficient maximum inner product search (MIPS) is performed using FAISS.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: DPR outperforms BM25 by 9-19% top-20 passage retrieval accuracy on Natural Questions and TriviaQA, achieving 78.4% top-20 accuracy on NQ.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
abstract: Language model pre-training embeds world knowledge implicitly. REALM augments LM pre-training with a learned neural retriever that retrieves documents from a Wikipedia corpus during pre-training.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: REALM models the retrieval of knowledge as a latent variable, propagating gradient updates into both the neural document retriever and the masked language model generator.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: REALM outperforms T5-11B on open-domain question answering benchmarks while using only 330M parameters.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: We explore general-purpose fine-tuning recipes for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: RAG models combine a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence model (BART) with a dense neural retriever (DPR) over a Wikipedia corpus. We explore RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token models for marginalizing retrieved passages.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: RAG sets state-of-the-art results on open-domain Natural Questions, WebQuestions, and CuratedTREC, while generating more factual and specific answers than parametric BART alone.

title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain QA (FiD)
abstract: Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD) performs evidence fusion in the decoder rather than the encoder, processing 100 retrieved passages independently in the encoder before cross-attention concatenation in the decoder.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: FiD passes each retrieved passage concatenated with the question through the T5 encoder independently, allowing linear encoder scaling with retrieved passages. The decoder then applies cross-attention over all passage representations simultaneously.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: FiD achieves 51.4 exact match on Natural Questions and 67.6 on TriviaQA, setting a new benchmark for generative open-domain QA.

title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
abstract: ColBERT introduces late interaction, encoding queries and documents into multi-vector token bags and computing max-similarity across token embeddings, retaining expressive cross-attention precision at vector search latency.

sections.heading: Late Interaction
sections.text: Instead of compressing an entire document into a single vector, ColBERT retains contextualized token embeddings and scores relevance using MaxSim: score(q, d) = sum_{i} max_{j} (E_Q(q)_i . E_D(d)_j).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: ColBERT achieves competitive MRR@10 with full cross-encoders on MS MARCO while retrieving over 100x faster.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
abstract: GraphRAG extracts a knowledge graph from raw text using LLMs, clusters entities into hierarchical communities, and generates multi-level summaries to answer global corpus-wide questions that vector RAG fails on.

sections.heading: Motivation
sections.text: Standard vector RAG fails when queries require synthesizing information across an entire corpus rather than retrieving local chunks. GraphRAG introduces hierarchical Leiden community detection over extracted knowledge graphs.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: GraphRAG achieves substantial gains over naive RAG on comprehensiveness, diversity, and global sense-making across multi-document corpora.

title: QA-GNN: Reasoning with Language Models and Knowledge Graphs for Question Answering
abstract: QA-GNN uses language models to score relevance of KG subgraphs and graph neural networks to perform relational multi-hop message passing.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: The model extracts a working subgraph from ConceptNet and joint trains a GNN with RoBERTa, fusing node representations via cross-attention.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Improves multi-hop reasoning accuracy on CommonsenseQA by 5.7% and OpenBookQA by 3.2%.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
abstract: We propose Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture, greatly reducing the number of trainable parameters for downstream tasks.

sections.heading: Problem & Hypothesis
sections.text: Fine-tuning all parameters of multi-billion parameter models is computationally prohibitive. We hypothesize that the change in weights during model adaptation has a low 'intrinsic dimension'.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: For a pre-trained weight matrix W_0 in R^{d x k}, LoRA constrains its update with a low-rank decomposition: W = W_0 + B A, where B in R^{d x r}, A in R^{r x k}, and rank r << min(d, k). When deployed, W_0 and BA can be folded with zero inference latency overhead.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: LoRA reduces trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory requirement by 3x compared to GPT-3 175B full fine-tuning, while achieving equal or better performance on GLUE, WikiSQL, and SAMSum.

title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP (Adapters)
abstract: Adapters inject small bottleneck feed-forward layers inside each Transformer sub-layer, training only 3% of parameters while preserving performance.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: Adapter modules consist of a bottleneck projection down to low dimension m, a non-linearity, and a projection back up to d, followed by a residual connection.

sections.heading: Tradeoffs
sections.text: While parameter efficient, adapter modules introduce sequential computation layers, increasing inference latency by 4-19%.

title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
abstract: Prefix-tuning keeps language model parameters frozen and prepends a sequence of continuous task-specific virtual tokens to key and value projections.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Prefix-tuning prepends l continuous vectors to the keys and values of every Transformer attention layer, training only 0.1% parameters.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.text: Outperforms adapters in low-data regimes and maintains performance on table-to-text generation.

title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: RAGAS is a framework for reference-free evaluation of RAG pipelines, defining metrics for faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, and context recall.

sections.heading: Metrics
sections.text: Faithfulness measures the ratio of claims in generated answers that can be inferred from context. Context Recall measures whether all ground truth sentences are covered by retrieved chunks.

sections.heading: Evaluation
sections.text: RAGAS metrics exhibit high correlation (Pearson r > 0.8) with human judgment on factual hallucination benchmarks.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG)
abstract: CRAG designs a lightweight retrieval evaluator to assess the quality of retrieved documents, triggering web search when retrieval confidence is low, and decomposing documents into fine-grained knowledge strips.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A retrieval evaluator classifies retrieval confidence into Correct, Ambiguous, or Incorrect, triggering self-correction actions accordingly.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Significantly improves factual accuracy across PopQA, Biography, and PubHealth benchmarks.
